# Skein 0.6 — full agent context

Skein is a small HTML-first runtime for native Web Components. Treat the browser DOM, Custom Elements, CSS, SVG, Canvas, Web Audio and other platform APIs as primary. Skein adds fine-grained reactive state, binding compilation, keyed DOM identity and scoped lifecycle.

## Component file model

`<user-card>` maps to `user/card.html`; hyphens become path separators and `.html` is appended. A component file may have top-level `<script>`, markup and `<style>`.

For inline demos:

```html
<hello-card></hello-card>
<template skein="hello-card">
  <script>this.name='world'</script>
  <b>Hello {name}</b>
</template>
```

Unknown tags are not eagerly claimed. Skein first fetches the matching HTML source; only a successful load causes `customElements.define`. A 404 leaves the tag undefined so another Web Components library can own it.

`Skein.define(tag, source)` is explicit registration for tooling/generated source and defines once. Redefinition throws. Production hot-reload instance registries/reload/generation machinery do not exist.

## Reactive state

Inside component scripts, `this` is a Proxy-backed state object.

Only arrays and plain/null-prototype objects are recursively reactive. Date, Map, Set, DOM nodes, AudioContext and class instances remain native objects and are not proxied. Their internal mutations are not automatically observable.

Reactive proxy/dependency registries are module-global WeakMaps. If the same raw object crosses component boundaries through a property input, both components see the same Skein Proxy rather than a proxy-of-proxy.

Reads track per raw-object/property dependency nodes. Missing own property reads track too. Binding lookup does not accept inherited prototype properties. Object enumeration tracks a dedicated structural dependency. Array growth/truncation notifies length/removed-index dependencies as needed. Failed Reflect writes/deletes do not notify.

## Paths and lookup

Bindings are strict dotted property paths. Examples: `count`, `user.name`, `items.0.title`, `$index`. Whitespace, empty segments, `{a + b}` and other expressions are compile errors.

Every binding path segment requires an own property. Missing keys on reactive proxies still track without reading inherited values. `each` creates an item BindingScope with local `index`/`$index`, then fallback walks outer item scopes to root. An own property with value `undefined` still shadows outer scopes.

There is no `in={...}` lexical-context feature in 0.6. Use explicit full paths outside list item scopes.

## Binding syntax

Text:

```html
<h1>{user.name}</h1>
```

String/native attributes:

```html
<div title="User {user.name}" data-id={id}></div>
<label for={inputId}>Name</label>
```

A full attribute binding removes the attribute for null/undefined/false.

DOM property:

```html
<input .value={name}>
```

Boolean attribute:

```html
<button ?disabled={saving}>Save</button>
```

Event:

```html
<button @click={save}>Save</button>
```

`.`, `?`, `@` forms require exactly one path and compile-time fail otherwise. Event handlers are invoked with the node as `this`, matching native listener semantics; prefer arrow handlers plus `event.currentTarget` in component scripts.

`<style>` contents are opaque to Skein parsing.

## Lists

```html
<li each={items} key={id}>
  {index}: {title}
</li>
```

Do not use old `for={items}` list syntax. `for` is left available to native dynamic attributes.

`ListPart` keeps key→record and ordered-record structures. It preflights keys before modifying record/view state. Explicit keys resolving null/undefined or duplicating another key throw. Existing records keep DOM/view identity, context and index refs update, removed records dispose, and surviving node ranges move with native `moveBefore()` when available or `insertBefore()` fallback.

Without an explicit key, object items use object identity. Primitive values use value+occurrence identity. Prefer explicit stable keys for application records.

## Conditions

```html
<section if={visible}>...</section>
```

A BranchPart owns a child Scope and one current View. Hide permanently disposes that view and removes its nodes; show instantiates a fresh view.

## Composition

Owner-to-child is native property assignment:

```html
<volume-control .value={volume}></volume-control>
```

Child declares:

```js
input('value', .5)
```

`input(name, fallback)` captures a pre-upgrade own property if present, otherwise fallback; deletes the temporary property; installs a host accessor backed by child state; seeds child state; lazily records the input; returns the initial value for compatibility with old `this.value = input(...)` syntax. Names colliding with `state` or inherited Skein/HTMLElement APIs throw.

Child-to-owner is native DOM events:

```js
host.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('value-change', {
  detail:{ value:this.value }, bubbles:true, composed:true
}))
```

No two-way binding, event bus, provide/inject or framework store is required for composition.

## Scheduler and computed/effects

`computed(fn)` returns a lazy cached ComputedRef that subscribes to dependencies read during computation. `effect(fn)` creates a user effect.

Synchronous writes enqueue one microtask. The scheduler always exhausts render effects before running one user effect, then returns to render effects if that user effect dirtied DOM work. This preserves settled-DOM-before-user-effect behavior.

There is no public `batch()`.

## Scope and lifecycle

Scope owns child scopes, effects/computed refs, cleanup callbacks and a lazily allocated AbortController.

`onCleanup(fn)` registers deterministic permanent cleanup. `abortSignal` is a lazily allocated Scope signal suitable for listeners/fetch.

Custom Element lifecycle:
- connect mounts once or resumes an existing paused view;
- disconnect pauses scope work;
- reconnect resumes dirty effects without rebuilding DOM;
- state-preserving platform moves can use connectedMoveCallback;
- `host.dispose()` permanently disposes and clears shadow DOM.

Mount is transactional. If template instantiation throws, the fresh Scope is disposed and partial shadow DOM is cleared before the error is reported.

Dynamic view teardown only force-disposes nested elements that are actual SkeinElement instances. Third-party custom elements rely on normal disconnected lifecycle; arbitrary `dispose()` methods on external elements are never called.

## Native objects

Prefer local variables for imperative browser resources:

```js
const audio = new AudioContext()
const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d')
```

They may also be stored in component state, but Skein returns them unchanged and does not observe internal mutation. Represent UI-observed values with normal reactive primitives/plain objects.

## Public surface

```js
Skein.version
Skein.define(tag, source)
```

Injected component script names:

```text
input
computed
effect
onCleanup
host
abortSignal
```

Do not invent `Skein.stats`, `Skein.flush`, `Skein.Signal`, `signal()`, `batch()`, `untrack()`, JSX expressions, SSR/hydration/suspense/error boundaries.

## Production build

`tools/build.mjs` concatenates readable modules, removes module syntax and lexically minifies/mangles known internals with zero dependencies. It is not an AST transform: identifier names that are native/public properties must not be added to the mangle map. Runtime source intentionally uses `hit['index']` and `controller['signal']` where necessary to avoid collisions. `dispose` must stay public.

Run `node tools/build.mjs`, `node tools/build.mjs --check`, `node test/run.mjs`.

The Chrome suite covers readable and minified runtime, 1000-row keyed identity, duplicate/missing keys, mount rollback, dynamic native `for`, third-party custom-element coexistence/disposal, input timing/collisions, shared Proxy identity, native Date/Map behavior, lifecycle, late define and real multi-file Skein Studio composition.

## 0.6 migration

```diff
- <li for={items} key={id}>...</li>
+ <li each={items} key={id}>...</li>

- <address in={user.address}>{city}</address>
+ <address>{user.address.city}</address>

- this.value = input('value', .5)
+ input('value', .5)
```

The input assignment form remains compatible. `for` list syntax and `in` contexts are intentionally removed.
